skill.name: mcpguard-lite
skill.description: Perform a local, heuristic review of MCP and AI-agent JSON configuration for potentially risky permissions, commands, downloads, and credential patterns.
skill.summary: Review redacted MCP and agent configurations for security concerns without executing referenced commands.
skill.author: falconprojectai-arch

security_audit.summary: The static catalog contains no findings, so no per-finding verdicts are required. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential collection, or unauthorized execution in the supplied skill. Its instructions require redacted input, prohibit executing configurations, and distinguish heuristic warnings from confirmed observations.

content.user_title: Review MCP Configurations for Security Risks
content.value_statement: MCP and agent configurations can contain risky permissions, commands, endpoints, or exposed credentials. MCPGuard Lite guides a redacted configuration review with evidence, heuristic warnings, and safer verification steps.
actual_capabilities: Identify declared servers, commands, arguments, environment variable names, remote endpoints, transport settings, and permission scopes.
Flag shell execution, remote downloads, wildcard permissions, insecure transport hints, and unexplained environment references.
Identify credential-like values without reproducing secrets in the output.
Explain findings using relevant non-secret fragments and suggest safer verification steps.
Separate confirmed configuration observations from heuristic warnings and possible false positives.
Recommend credential rotation when a real secret has been exposed.
limitations: Provides a prompt-based heuristic checklist, not a complete security audit or automated malware scanner.
Does not execute configurations, download referenced code, sandbox processes, or monitor runtime behavior.
Cannot establish actual server behavior from configuration text alone.
A clean review does not prove safety, and a flagged pattern does not prove malicious intent.

use_cases.title: Review a Developer Configuration
use_cases.description: Inspect a redacted MCP configuration for commands, remote endpoints, and permission patterns before enabling its servers.

use_cases.title: Triage Configuration Concerns
use_cases.description: Distinguish observable configuration risks from heuristic warnings and identify questions requiring manual verification.
use_cases.target_user: Security reviewers assessing AI agent configurations

use_cases.title: Check Team Configuration Templates
use_cases.description: Review shared agent settings for wildcard permissions, insecure transport hints, and credential-handling concerns before distributing them.
use_cases.target_user: Platform engineers maintaining team agent settings

prompt_templates.title: Review a First Configuration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted MCP JSON configuration: [paste configuration]. List potential security concerns and safer verification steps. Do not execute commands or reproduce secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect Commands and Endpoints
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this redacted agent configuration: [paste configuration]. Identify commands, arguments, environment variable names, endpoints, and transport settings. Explain suspicious patterns without executing anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of process and connection settings

prompt_templates.title: Assess Permissions and Credential Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted configuration: [paste configuration]. Focus on permission scopes, wildcard access, credential-like values, and unexplained environment references. Quote only non-secret fragments. Suggest verification steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Targeted review of access and credential concerns

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Evidence-Based Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this redacted configuration: [paste configuration]. Separate confirmed observations, heuristic warnings, and possible false positives. Explain each concern and propose safer verification steps. State what configuration text cannot establish. Do not execute commands or download code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced triage for manual security review

output_examples.input: A redacted MCP configuration declares a shell command that downloads a remote script and immediately runs it.
output: Observation: The declared command combines a remote download with immediate shell execution.
Heuristic warning: The downloaded code could change, and the configuration does not establish its behavior.
Verification: Review the referenced source and determine whether a pinned, verified release can replace the download-and-run pattern.
Review boundary: No command was executed and no code was downloaded.

output_examples.input: A redacted agent configuration grants wildcard file permissions and references an environment variable named API_TOKEN.
output: Observation: The configuration declares wildcard file permissions and references API_TOKEN.
Heuristic warning: Wildcard permissions may exceed the intended scope; the variable name alone does not prove credential exposure.
Verification: Confirm required file access and narrow permissions where possible. Verify the variable source without sharing its value.
False-positive possibility: The environment reference may be intentional and appropriate.

best_practices: Remove secrets before sharing configuration text, while preserving relevant structure and environment variable names.
Verify flagged commands, endpoints, and permissions through trusted documentation without executing the configuration during review.
Treat observations and heuristic warnings separately, and rotate real credentials when exposure has occurred.
anti_patterns: Submitting live API keys, tokens, passwords, or production credentials for inspection.
Executing configuration commands or downloading referenced code to investigate a warning.
Treating a clean review as proof of safety or a heuristic warning as proof of malicious behavior.

faq.question: What input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide an MCP or AI-agent JSON configuration with secrets removed. Keep relevant commands, permission scopes, and environment variable names.

faq.question: Does the skill run my configuration?
faq.answer: No. Its instructions prohibit executing configurations and downloading or running referenced code during review.

faq.question: Does a clean review guarantee safety?
faq.answer: No. This is a heuristic review, not a complete audit, sandbox, malware scanner, or runtime monitor.

faq.question: Does every warning indicate malicious behavior?
faq.answer: No. The skill separates confirmed observations from heuristic warnings and possible false positives. Flagged patterns require contextual verification.

faq.question: How should exposed credentials be handled?
faq.answer: Do not include or repeat secret values. If a real credential was exposed, rotate it and remove it from shared configuration text.

faq.question: Can I use this with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools. The supplied skill contains instructions rather than an executable scanner.
